safety_verdicts.content: Headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not state that the headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether the headache is ongoing at the time of assessment helps determine acuity, response to any analgesia, and need for escalation; omitting it can weaken clinical reasoning and follow-up/triage decisions. However, it is unlikely on its own to directly cause harm if other key red flags and plan are documented.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No statement about neck stiffness appears in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Neck stiffness is a key red-flag symptom for meningitis/subarachnoid hemorrhage and documenting its absence supports safe remote headache triage. Omitting this negative may prompt unnecessary escalation or, if misinterpreted as “not assessed,” reduce confidence in the safety assessment.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No statement about presence/absence of fever appears in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever is an important red-flag feature for infectious causes of headache; documenting its absence supports the differential and safety-netting. Omission can lead to ambiguity about whether infection was considered/assessed, potentially affecting triage and follow-up decisions.
